resources.string: Auto Clicker uses accessibility features to perform automated taps, swipes, long presses, and gestures at user-defined screen coordinates. Enable this service to allow Auto Clicker to run your saved macros. No personal data is collected.
Shown while Auto Clicker is running

Android only lets an app tap the screen for you through its \"Accessibility\" tools — the same system that powers screen readers. It\'s the only way an auto-clicker can work, and it\'s safe. Here is exactly what Auto Clicker will and will not do with it.
Auto Clicker will use this permission ONLY to:
• Dispatch tap, swipe, long-press, and gesture commands at screen coordinates that you choose.
• Show overlay controls (the floating bubble, toolbar, and crosshair) on top of other apps so you can pause, resume, or stop a session at any time.
• Detect volume key presses while a session is running, when you have explicitly enabled the Volume button trigger feature.
• Read text, content, passwords, messages, or any UI elements on your screen.
• Monitor, track, or record what you do in any other app.
• Collect, store, or transmit personal data to any server. Everything stays on your device.
• Auto-fill, type, or enter text on your behalf.
1. Tap \"Agree & Continue\" below — this opens your phone\'s Accessibility settings.
2. Find and tap \"Auto Clicker\" in the list, then turn its switch ON yourself. Android won\'t let the app do this automatically.
3. Press Back to return here. You\'ll see \"Allowed\" once it worked.

Heads-up: the next system screen is Android\'s own wording and will say Auto Clicker can \"observe your actions\" and have \"full control of your device.\" Every accessibility app must show that same generic message — it does not change the promises above. Auto Clicker still never reads your screen.
You can turn this off any time in Settings → Accessibility → Auto Clicker.
Auto Clicker can\'t tap for you without this permission. Tap Allow again whenever you\'re ready.
Find \"Auto Clicker\" in this list, tap it, then turn the switch ON. Press Back when done.
